scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: My mom left me in charge because she wasn't coming home until 1 AM. She trusted me and my friend, so I let my friend over. I made sure my brother went to bed on time because he can put himself to bed. But then he woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us. I told him to go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. I was worried that if I tried to force him, he'd throw a fit, which would be embarrassing and exhausting. So I let him stay, and by the time the movie ended, he was almost asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him to bed around midnight. The next morning, he didn't want to get up and was cranky. My mom knew I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7, he should know about consequences and that staying up later would make him feel bad. I also told her that missing two hours of sleep isn't a big deal for a kid his age. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by not forcing him to bed. Let me consider the pros and cons. Pros of letting him stay: - He was already awake and wouldn't go back to sleep easily. - My friend was there, and he's a positive influence; he's cute and hype him up. - Forcing him might have led to a tantrum, which would have been stressful for everyone. - He ended up falling asleep during the movie, so he still got some sleep, just later. Cons of letting him stay: - He missed two hours of sleep, which might affect his mood and behavior the next day. - It sets a precedent that he can stay up late if he wants, which might lead to more issues with bedtime in the future. - My mom was upset because she trusted me to enforce the bedtime rules. I also need to think about the bigger picture. My brother is sensitive to sleep, so even a little less can make him cranky. But he's 7, and part of growing up is learning about consequences. Maybe he should understand that staying up late means he'll feel tired the next day. On the other hand, I didn't want to cause a scene by dragging him upstairs, which could have been stressful for everyone, including my friend. Plus, he ended up sleeping during the movie, so he did get some rest, just later than usual. I also told my mom that two hours isn't a big deal, but maybe she thinks it is because she knows how sensitive he is. She might be concerned about setting a precedent or about the importance of consistent bedtime routines. So, was it right or wrong? I think it's a bit of both. Letting him stay was kind and considerate in the moment, but it might not have been the best decision in terms of teaching him about consequences and maintaining a consistent routine. However, considering the immediate situation and avoiding a tantrum, it might have been the better choice at the time. I guess the key points are: 1. Immediate consequences: Avoiding a tantrum and keeping the mood positive. 2. Long-term consequences: Teaching him about responsibility and consistent bedtime. 3. The impact on the next day: He was cranky, which shows that missing sleep affected him. In the end, I think it's a judgment call. While it's important to teach him about consequences, it's also important to handle the situation in a way that maintains peace and avoids unnecessary stress. Maybe next time, I can find a middle ground, like setting a specific time for him to go to bed or having a calming activity after the movie ends.
